prompt: A finished graphic design poster, seen flat-on and full bleed; the image is the poster itself, not a mockup on a wall. Printed in flat solid inks on uncoated off-white paper, four inks at most: signal red, cobalt blue, black, and the off-white paper as the ground. Four huge heavy bold black sans-serif words are stacked down the poster, left-aligned, filling the width, one word per row in this order: "BAR", "BAKERY", "WARD", "BED". Each word has a solid cobalt blue extruded side dropping down and to the right, a hard-edged flat shadow plane, so the words stand like four blocks of a building. One single transit-map line in signal red, of one fixed thick width, enters from the top edge of the poster and runs down through the four words, bending only at 90 and 45 degrees with one consistent corner radius. It passes through the letters, and at each word it stops at a station: a white circle with a thick black ring placed exactly inside the closed hole of a letter: inside the hole of the A in BAR, the hole of the A in BAKERY, the hole of the D in WARD, and the hole of the D in BED. After the station in BED the red line runs straight down and leaves through the bottom edge of the poster. In the top right corner, small but bold, the line's name "N7" in black inside a signal red circle. Flat vector screen print, crisp edges, no gradients, no glow, no gloss, no bevels, no soft shadows; depth only from the hard-edged cobalt extrusions. Every word spelled exactly: "BAR", "BAKERY", "WARD", "BED", "N7". No other text, no small print, no logos, no placeholder text, no people, no map texture.

At the foot of the post, very small, under one-tenth of the poster's height, one tiny person built from simple geometric shapes: a sun yellow coat, black trousers, a circle head, standing and waiting. Hard-edged shapes, flat vector screen print, no gradients, no glow, no gloss, no bevels, no soft shadows, no stars, no moon, no street lamps. Every word spelled exactly: "BOTH WAYS", "ALL NIGHT".
